title: 2nd Mystery The Ease Of Essential Power

questions.question: What main idea does this passage teach about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah’s power handles countless things as easily as one thing, and nothing is hard for Him.

questions.question: How is Allah’s power described in relation to light?
questions.answer: It is described as the finest and highest light, above all other lights.

questions.question: What are things compared to because of their inner nature?
questions.answer: They are compared to bright mirrors.

questions.question: Which kinds of created things are mentioned to show how wide Allah’s command reaches?
questions.answer: The passage mentions tiny things like atoms, living things like plants and animals, and huge heavenly bodies like stars, suns, and moons.

questions.question: What attitude do all created things have toward Allah’s command in this passage?
questions.answer: They are fully obedient and submit to it.

questions.question: Why does the passage say it is natural for many things to be created as easily as one?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s power is perfect, luminous, and unlimited, and all things obey His command.

questions.question: What does the passage say about one task interfering with another?
questions.answer: It says no task gets in the way of another for Allah’s power.

questions.question: What pairs of opposites are listed to show that all are equal before Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Great and small, many and few, and particular and universal.

questions.question: What example is used to show that something huge can be moved by a very small cause under a system of order?
questions.answer: A very large ship is moved the way a child moves a toy with a finger.

questions.question: What does the example of the commander and the army show?
questions.answer: It shows that one command can direct either one soldier or a whole army with equal ease.

questions.question: In the balance example, what happens when a tiny object is added?
questions.answer: Even a tiny object can make one side rise and the other fall if the balance is set properly.

questions.question: What point is the balance example meant to teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that under Allah’s wise law, very great things can be directed with ease and precision.

questions.question: According to the passage, what stands behind order, regularity, and balance in creation?
questions.answer: Allah’s justice and endless wisdom within His eternal power.

questions.question: How does the passage compare moving stars with moving atoms?
questions.answer: It says Allah moves the stars just as easily as He moves atoms.

questions.question: How does the passage compare giving life to one fly and to all flies and many other living things?
questions.answer: It says Allah gives life to one fly and to whole groups of living things with the same ease and command.

questions.question: What happens in spring that is compared to bringing a tree to life?
questions.answer: Allah revives the earth and brings forth huge numbers of living examples, similar to resurrection.

questions.question: What can a student infer from the passage about size and number in relation to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Size and number do not limit Allah at all, because the biggest and the smallest are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: What is the central message of this passage?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that Allah’s eternal power works with complete ease over everything, whether one thing or many things.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the power of Allah’s essence?
questions.answer: It describes it as pure, exalted, and brighter than every other light.

questions.question: Why are the inner realities of things compared to mirrors?
questions.answer: Because they are presented as able to receive and display the effects of Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the obedience of creation?
questions.answer: It says all created things are under Allah’s command and follow it completely.

questions.question: Which examples show that both tiny and huge things are included under this command?
questions.answer: Atoms, plants, animals, stars, suns, and moons.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is creating many things at once not a problem?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s power is unlimited and no work blocks another.

questions.question: What statement in the passage shows that Allah’s power is not strained by variety?
questions.answer: The passage says that the large and the small, the many and the few, and the particular and the universal are all the same for that power.

questions.question: What everyday image is used to explain how a huge object may be moved under proper order?
questions.answer: A child pushing a toy is used to explain it.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of one soldier and a full army receiving one command?
questions.answer: The same command can direct both little and much when there is full obedience.

questions.question: In the example of the scale, why is the walnut important?
questions.answer: It shows that even a very small addition can bring a big change when the system is balanced.

questions.question: What quality of Allah’s power is connected to order and balance?
questions.answer: His justice and wisdom are connected to order and balance.

questions.question: How does the passage connect wisdom with the motion of the stars?
questions.answer: It says the stars move through the wisdom of Allah’s order.

questions.question: What comparison is made between stars and atoms?
questions.answer: Both are moved by Allah with equal ease.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Allah giving life in spring?
questions.answer: He gives life to one small creature and to whole groups of living things through the same command and with the same ease.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the earth in spring?
questions.answer: It describes the earth as being brought back to life after being like a corpse.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect idea runs through the whole passage?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s power is wise, just, eternal, and obeyed by all things, He creates and governs everything easily.

questions.question: What does this passage mainly explain about Allah’s power and creation?
questions.answer: It explains that Allah creates and controls all things with perfect ease, no matter how many or how large they are.

questions.question: What special description is given to Allah’s eternal power?
questions.answer: It is described as the purest and most excellent light.

questions.question: How are created things presented in relation to that power?
questions.answer: They are shown as reflective and ready to receive its command.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the behavior of all created things toward Allah’s orders?
questions.answer: They submit completely and act in obedience.

questions.question: Why does the passage include both atoms and heavenly bodies in one sentence?
questions.answer: To show that Allah’s command covers everything from the smallest to the greatest.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes creating countless things side by side completely fitting?
questions.answer: Allah’s perfect power and the obedience of all things make it fully fitting and easy.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about distractions or competing tasks for Allah?
questions.answer: There are none; one work does not interrupt another.

questions.question: What groups of words are used to show that all categories are equal before Allah’s power?
questions.answer: The passage mentions large and small, many and few, and individual and general.

questions.question: Why is the image of a giant ship moved like a toy important?
questions.answer: It helps the reader imagine how easy great actions are when directed by perfect order.

questions.question: What does the military example add to the main idea?
questions.answer: It shows that one command can direct either one person or many people without needing a different kind of order.

questions.question: How does the scale example increase the strength of the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that when a law and balance are in place, even a tiny cause can affect something enormous.

questions.question: What two qualities of Allah are named as the source of order and balance?
questions.answer: Divine justice and endless wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage connect these qualities to creation?
questions.answer: It says all regularity and equilibrium in creation come from them.

questions.question: What comparison is made between reviving a fly and reviving larger groups of creatures?
questions.answer: Both are done by Allah with the same command and equal ease.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah sends out onto the plain of life in spring?
questions.answer: He sends out the species of flies and the many groups of plants and animals.

questions.question: How is reviving a tree related to reviving the earth?
questions.answer: The passage says both are done with Allah’s wise and just power, and both are easy for Him.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the earth as a corpse suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests the earth seems dead before spring, then Allah brings it back to life.

questions.question: What truth about Allah is emphasized all through this passage?
questions.answer: His power is absolute, and nothing in creation is difficult for Him.

questions.question: How is Allah’s power described using the image of light?
questions.answer: It is presented as the most refined and highest light.

questions.question: What image is used for the inner sides of created things?
questions.answer: They are pictured as shining mirrors.

questions.question: What do those mirror-like things do in relation to Allah’s command?
questions.answer: They stand under it in full obedience and submission.

questions.question: Why does the passage list so many different kinds of things, from atoms to moons?
questions.answer: To show that every level of creation is included under the same power.

questions.question: What does the passage say about creating many things next to each other?
questions.answer: It says this happens with the same ease as creating one thing.

questions.question: What claim is made about different tasks before Allah?
questions.answer: One task never keeps Him from another.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying the particular and the universal are the same for Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It means an individual thing and a broad group are equally easy for Him to handle.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the example of the large ship and the child’s toy?
questions.answer: It shows that huge movements can happen simply under proper command and order.

questions.question: How does the commander example support the same idea?
questions.answer: It shows that one instruction can send either one soldier or a whole army into action.

questions.question: In the balance example, what matters more than the size of the object added?
questions.answer: The system of balance and the law governing it matter more.

questions.question: What lesson does that give about Allah’s way of acting in creation?
questions.answer: Allah acts through perfect wisdom and order, so even enormous results come about easily.

questions.question: Which features of Allah’s power are named directly near the middle of the passage?
questions.answer: It is called absolute, infinite, luminous, essential, and eternal.

questions.question: What role do justice and wisdom play in the passage?
questions.answer: They are the basis of order, regularity, and balance in creation.

questions.question: How are stars and atoms used in comparison?
questions.answer: The passage says Allah moves the stars just as easily as He moves atoms.

questions.question: What is compared with giving life to a single fly?
questions.answer: Giving life to all flies and to many plants and animals is compared with it.

questions.question: How does the passage connect spring to resurrection?
questions.answer: Spring is shown as a wide display of life returning, like many small examples of resurrection.

questions.question: What should students learn from the final image of the earth in spring?
questions.answer: They should learn that Allah can bring life back on a vast scale with complete ease.

questions.question: What is the big message of the target passage in simple words?
questions.answer: Allah can do everything easily, whether it is one thing or countless things.

questions.question: What comparison does the passage use for Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It compares it to the highest and purest light.

questions.question: What comparison does the passage use for the realities of created things?
questions.answer: It compares them to shining mirrors.

questions.question: What do all created things have in common in this passage?
questions.answer: They all obey Allah’s command.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention atoms, plants, animals, stars, suns, and moons together?
questions.answer: To show that all creation, small and great, is under one power.

questions.question: What does the passage say about making many things together?
questions.answer: It says making many things together is as easy as making one.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the relationship between different divine tasks?
questions.answer: It says they do not block or confuse one another.

questions.question: Which contrasts are listed to stress that Allah’s power is not limited?
questions.answer: Big and small, many and few, and specific and broad things.

questions.question: What is the point of the giant ship example?
questions.answer: It shows that something very large can be directed easily through order.

questions.question: What is the point of the commander giving one order?
questions.answer: It shows that one order can move either one soldier or many soldiers.

questions.question: What does the scale with mountains teach the reader?
questions.answer: It teaches that under a precise law, a small cause can produce a huge result.

questions.question: What are the roots of order and balance in creation according to the passage?
questions.answer: They come from Allah’s justice and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the stars and atoms?
questions.answer: Allah moves both with equal ease.

questions.question: In spring, what does Allah do for one fly and for the whole species?
questions.answer: He gives life to both through the same command and with the same ease.

questions.question: Besides flies, what other living things are mentioned as receiving life in spring?
questions.answer: Plants and animals are also mentioned.

questions.question: What happens to the earth in spring according to the passage?
questions.answer: Allah revives it after it is like a dead body.

questions.question: What are the many springtime revivals called in meaning?
questions.answer: They are presented as many examples that point to resurrection.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the difficulty level of Allah’s actions?
questions.answer: It teaches that nothing is difficult for Allah’s power.

questions.question: How is Allah’s eternal power pictured at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It is pictured as the most excellent and subtle light.

questions.question: How are the essences of things pictured?
questions.answer: They are pictured as bright mirrors.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the response of all things to Allah’s command?
questions.answer: All things are obedient and under His authority.

questions.question: What range of creation is named to show this authority?
questions.answer: The passage names the smallest things, living things, and the great bodies in the sky.

questions.question: Why does the passage say creating endless things together is natural?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s power is unlimited and the whole creation submits to it.

questions.question: What statement shows that Allah never faces overload?
questions.answer: The passage says one matter does not interfere with another.

questions.question: What teaching is given by saying great and small are alike for Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It teaches that size makes no difference to Him.

questions.question: What teaching is given by saying many and few are alike for Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It teaches that number does not make anything harder for Him.

questions.question: What does the image of a child moving a toy help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand that huge things can be moved easily under Allah’s order.

questions.question: How does the example of a commander’s order deepen that understanding?
questions.answer: It shows that one command can govern either one or many without any added difficulty.

questions.question: Why is the example of the balanced mountains important?
questions.answer: It shows that when perfect law and balance exist, very large masses can be affected through a small cause.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the source of all order and regularity in creation?
questions.answer: It comes from Allah’s justice and endless wisdom within His eternal power.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the movement of stars and atoms?
questions.answer: It says both are moved with the same ease.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah giving life in spring?
questions.answer: He gives life to one small creature and to whole groups of creatures equally easily.

questions.question: What broad groups are brought to life in spring besides one species of fly?
questions.answer: The many hosts of plants and animals are also brought to life.

questions.question: How does the passage connect a tree and the whole earth?
questions.answer: It says Allah gives life to a tree and also revives the earth with equal ease through His wise and just power.
